label: Editorial Review
title: The Sky-Fallen Legacy: The AI Series That Made Viewers Forget About AI
excerpt: An expanding alien world and recurring characters. Reality Foundry Studio's independent sci-fi series is giving viewers something to discuss beyond the fact that it was made with AI.
heroCaption: Ethan and Sheila in The Sky-Fallen Legacy. Image: Reality Foundry Studio.
body: AI generated film making was always about what could a model produce. Can we create a human? An other world? A action sequence? With Reality Foundry Studios release of Sky-Fallen Legacy they ask the question. Can we make something that will have viewers wanting more. So far it looks like the answer is yes. People are discussing choices made by characters and hoping for character reunions and getting upset when the episode ends too quick. Yes AI is still involved in this discussion but it doesn't have to be all of it.

When our story starts we meet Ethan he is a Human engineer who his ship has become trapped in an anomaly and crashes onto a new planet. He meets Sheila who is a Sirta and is introduced to there ways and how they are split up as well as there hostility towards humans. While on another side of the universe Jack and Eva (who is a synthetic) are searching for their lost friend. This expands the universe for the show and gives more background on the politics and technology used in this world. But that is all you need to know going into this. Enjoy how both plots play out.

The closest thing to compare this too would be Avatar. You have an alien race who are different then us and the story is about his bond to them and trying to save their world that he knows little about. With the different races fighting each other and old lore I would also say its similar to Lord of the rings. On the other hand its kind of like Mass Effect. Ships and space related organizations, people choosing sides and A.I's. These are all just similarities to there styles of stories. The Sky-Fallen Legacy takes the good from many types of stories and brings them together.

Ethan isn't just a man with cool tech he's also an engineer that has to decide what he will do to stay alive. While sheila helps ground the story on earth. With her love and interest for the planet and ethan.

These images are taken from different episodes but you can still pick out both characters and their traits. Having this type of continuity throughout your clips and episodes is something that has become possible with today's character reference and ai generated video techniques. It could be done but there's no way of knowing how these were made.

Many of these comments dont even relate to the realism aspect. They pick there favorite characters and follow along with the side plots and worry about what happens next. One thing that makes this series enjoyable is eva becoming more emotional its almost like a typical robot show plot but we care about what happens.

It's good to have Netflix as a comparison when talking about how big these shows can get. Netflix's 3 Body Problem was said to have cost around $160M for it's 8 episode run. Their netflix report showed that they had 445.2M hours watched in 2024 which is about 60.1M people watching the entire show.

There is no information on what the sky-fallen legacy cost to produce or any similar number of hours watched. We can't claim that we're at par with Netflix. But could we use generated technology to help lower the price of creating a world while still giving the audience what they enjoy?

Of course not its a perfect show. People have brought up some questionable choices that characters made. There's been some odd continuity issues here and there and unrealistic action sequences as well. The show creator addressed the comments about the subtitles in episode 12 and said they will not be doing that again. All valid criticism to point out about the show. Not to mention that we are now nitpicking about the story and how the show was directed which is a good thing.

With good imagery and characters that keep appearing you can create something with the use of AI. Such as what we saw in Sky-Fallen Legacy. There is no doubt that AI can allow someone to make something big. But you still need that human touch to get people invested.
